summary: Built all three parts of the design. The argv repair is `CommandLine.Arguments` plus `Kernel32.CommandLineAsTyped`, wired into `App.OnStartup` before the `--report` test. The SC-028 up-front probe and SC-037 exclusive-create temporary both live in the new `ReportFile`, which `StartReportMode`, `WindowReport.WriteAsync` and the crash handler now use. The slice's repro now exits 0. The whole suite is 1443 of 1443 (baseline 1389), and the bug project's 5 facts pass. On the published single-file exe the trailing-backslash line gives the same report as the control (536 files) through Start-Process and cmd /c; the spaced root with a two-space report folder lands at the exact path. `"C:\" --report C:\r.json` now exits 3 in 143 ms with no window and no scan. The engine's leftover state was kept where right and finished (the repro test and its csproj). The fitness block was replaced with one hand-written SL-007 block of three rules (m7).

WriteAsync takes a ReportFile and ends with file.Write(json). Discard and DeleteQuietly removed (their only caller was App). Exit 3 remark now says an unwritable folder is refused before the scan.

ReportFileTests.AFailedMoveLeavesNoTemporary: <report> held open without FileShare.Delete, Write throws, no `.fsa-*` entry remains, and the held file is intact.

Stem timing: the constructor stores only the Func, Probe and Write each draw on the line before their own open, and the counting-Func fact checks draws 0/1/2 and that nothing was on disk at either draw. Facts for finish lines 2, 3 and 4 are in the bug project (QuotedRootShapesTests, AppRun), and line 2 creates `out  dir` first. The measurement opened the build: the repro and the exe facts ran on the Debug apphost first, then on the published single-file exe (in a spaced folder), through Start-Process and cmd /c. Alignment held on every line, so no resynthesis. Breaking alignment gives exit 2 and a red repro, which is what the design predicted.

Rule 1 is now `(?m)(?<!CommandLine\.Arguments\()\b\w+\.Args\b`, `(?m)\bGetCommandLineArgs\b` and `(?m)[{,]\s*Args\s*[:.]` (a superset of the critic's property pattern). Rule 3 bans StreamWriter, FileStream, File.Open/OpenHandle and the parameterless .Create/.OpenWrite/.CreateText/.AppendText() outside ReportFile.cs (except_files), beside the File.* and FileMode patterns. deviations: No settings checkbox or notice was built for the argv repair. I judged the Windows argument rule not to be an outside defect: it is documented, by-design behaviour (rust#72653 and others closed as expected), and the repair is this app's own command-line grammar, decided in the design (an odd backslash run before a quote is kept whole). The same goes for GetCommandLineW over the rebuilt Environment.CommandLine, which is picking the right API and not a precaution with a cost. Arguments are parsed before any window or setting exists, and unattended runs have none. If a reviewer reads the merged argument as an outside defect, the switch and notice are still owed.

Rule 1's third pattern is `[{,]\s*Args\s*[:.]`, a superset of the critic's `\{\s*Args\s*:`. It also catches extended property patterns (`{ Args.Length: > 0 }`) and a property second in a pattern. Rule 3 also bans `File.OpenHandle` (`\bFile\.Open(Handle)?\s*\(`), beyond the critic's list.

Added two corpora and a test the design did not list: ReportFilePlantsCorpus.json, SettledRulesCorpus.json and SettledRulesCorpusTests. The CLOSE-THE-CLASS obligations (O-020, O-023, O-024, O-043) ask for corpora and a demonstration of the code failing before the fix; SettledRulesCorpusTests reads the patterns from .taad/fitness.yaml, so there is one copy.

ReportFileTests' link facts are corpus-driven Theories with more members than the design named: directory symlink, file and folder at the temporary, three earlier-stem rows, a dangling symlink at <report>, and a dangling symlink at the legacy name.

Only the four WindowCases leftover checks the design named (C-007, C-008, C-012, O-016) use Test-NoReportTemporary. The other `.tmp` checks (C-008's stale-.tmp ones, C-009 and the folder-gone-mid-scan one) are unchanged.
not_built: tests/window/WindowMutants.ps1 NoCrashHandler and NoExitRule mutants were not run; I confirmed only that their two App.xaml.cs regexes still match exactly once each. C-012 and O-016 pass unmutated.

The Python Fitness engine (taad3/fitness.py) and eng/rules-harness/harness.py need the external engine and could not be run here. The three rules were checked with .NET regex through SettledRulesCorpusTests (patterns read from fitness.yaml, 56 corpus rows, and the App's source in raw text, comments included, which is stricter than the engine's code-only match).
follow_ups: m5 stays deferred: hold a handle to the report folder from launch without FILE_SHARE_DELETE, or compare GetFinalPathNameByHandle at launch and at write, so a junction swap of the folder mid-scan cannot redirect the rename-over.
The dotnet-muxer launch (`dotnet app.dll "X\" --report f`) falls back by design (exit 2, or RootArgument for a trailing-only quote); it is covered by unit rows but was not launched end to end.

tests/window/FsaWindowHook/TreeMode.cs:99 still tests `Environment.GetCommandLineArgs().Contains("--report")`. It only refuses misuse and its launches are quoted by Format-AppArgument, so it is unaffected, but it is the one other reader of unrepaired arguments, outside rule 1's src/FsAnalyser.App scope.
